html:
The Byzantine civil war of 1341 to 1347 was fought over who would rule for the nine-year-old emperor John V Palaiologos after his father Andronikos III died. It ruined what was left of the Byzantine Empire.

On one side was John Kantakouzenos, the late emperor's friend and chief minister, backed by the great landowners. On the other was a regency of the empress-mother Anna of Savoy, the patriarch John Kalekas and the admiral Alexios Apokaukos, with much of the townspeople behind them. In Thessalonica a popular party, the Zealots, seized power and ran the city for years.

Both sides hired foreign troops. Kantakouzenos brought in the Serbs of Stefan Dušan, who used the chance to conquer Macedonia, and then the Turks of the Ottoman ruler Orhan, who married his daughter. Turkish armies plundered Thrace. Kantakouzenos entered Constantinople in 1347 and ruled as co-emperor. The war left the countryside wrecked and the treasury empty, and the Black Death struck the same year. Soon the Ottomans took Gallipoli and crossed into Europe.
